verdict.rationale: iTerm2's AI features ship as a separate optional plugin, built so terminal data cannot be accidentally sent over the network. Community reports say the feature is off by default, needs your own API key, and sends nothing until you ask a question. A configurable API URL may also allow local models such as Ollama. That keeps your data away from model trainers by default, but there is no explicit statement on training use, and once enabled, training is governed by whichever provider you choose. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party policy that user data is never used for training, a documented clear off-toggle (users note any value in the key field activates it), first-party documentation of local-model support, and independent verification of what is transmitted.
